title: Intrinsic proper/open alpha base-change equation on module sheaves
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For each scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $P_f$ for the specified inverse-image functor [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], $L_j$ for exact open extension [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], and $\alpha(k,r,p,i;h):P_pL_i\to L_kP_r$ for the intrinsic ordinary clopen map [def-cbc-strict-tower-ordinary-proper-open-arrows]. The arrows in the following equations include the specified inverse-image compositors $c^P_{f,g}:P_{gf}\cong P_fP_g$, the unit-preserving open compositors $c^L_{i,j}:L_jL_i\cong L_{ji}$, and the cartesian open comparison $\beta$ [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. Let $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$, $k_1:V_1\hookrightarrow W_1$, and $i_1:S_1\hookrightarrow T_1$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$, $r_1:V_1\to S_1$, $p_1:W_1\to T_1$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $a:W_1\to W$, $b:T_1\to T$, $c:S_1\to S$, and $d:V_1\to V$ satisfy $pk=ir$, $p_1k_1=i_1r_1$, $kd=ak_1$, $ic=bi_1$, $pa=bp_1$, $rd=cr_1$. Assume each of the four side squares $(d,k_1,k,a)$, $(c,i_1,i,b)$, $(a,p_1,p,b)$, and $(d,r_1,r,c)$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\sigma_p:P_{p_1}P_b\cong P_aP_p$ and $\sigma_r:P_{r_1}P_c\cong P_dP_r$ be the canonical inverse-image square identifications. For every module sheaf $M$ on $S$,
$$L_{k_1}((\sigma_r^{-1})_M)\circ (\beta_k)_{P_rM}\circ P_a(\alpha(k,r,p,i)_M)\circ(\sigma_p)_{L_iM}=\alpha(k_1,r_1,p_1,i_1)_{P_cM}\circ P_{p_1}((\beta_i)_M).$$
This assertion is on module sheaves only; the original proper/open square need not be cartesian.

proof.text: Work first with module sheaves, writing $P_u=u^{-1}$ and $L_j=j_!$. Restriction detects maps with target $L_jM$ for every quasi-compact open $j$, as follows. For two maps $f,g:F\to L_jM$ with $P_jf=P_jg$, let $I=\operatorname{im}(f-g)$. Exact inverse image gives $P_jI=0$. If $z$ is the complementary closed immersion, exact inverse image applied to $I\hookrightarrow L_jM$ gives $P_zI\hookrightarrow P_zL_jM=0$. The short exact open/closed sequence for $I$ now has both outside terms zero, hence $I=0$ and $f=g$. Here apply the ringed open/closed lemma with $A=\underline B_X$; its pulled-back coefficients are the canonical constant rings. All opens to which detection will be applied are quasi-compact, including composite and base-changed opens.

Record explicitly the normalization of the cartesian comparison. The open-unit beta lemma [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization] gives, for arbitrary $B$ and already on module sheaves, that the transpose below is invertible with inverse $\beta$, natural and with the stated compositor laws; the definition fixes this transpose. For a cartesian square with opens $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and maps $a:X'\to X$, $v:U'\to U$, write $\sigma:P_vP_j\cong P_{j'}P_a$ for the specified pullback-square isomorphism and $u_j:1\cong P_jL_j$ for the open unit. The definition of $\beta^{-1}:L_{j'}P_v\to P_aL_j$ as the transpose says
$$P_{j'}(\beta^{-1}_M)u_{j',P_vM}=\sigma_{L_jM}P_v(u_{j,M}).$$
Inverting gives
$$u_{j',P_vM}^{-1}P_{j'}(\beta_M)=P_v(u_{j,M}^{-1})\sigma_{L_jM}^{-1}.$$
Thus restriction of beta is precisely the canonical identification obtained from the inverse-image compositor and the open units. This calculation uses no coefficient finiteness. Below identify $P_jL_j$ with $1$ by this particular unit; all suppressed comparisons are the specified inverse-image compositors or their unit-preserving open-adjoint conjugates.

For any of the proper/open squares let $s:V\hookrightarrow W_S$ be its lift. The clopen-projector statement identifies the intrinsic alpha with $L_b\pi_sP_q\circ\beta_{i,p}$ and gives $P_s\pi_s=1$. Restricting along $k=bs$, step 2 cancels the cartesian beta and the open units, and $P_s\pi_s=1$ cancels the remaining projector. Consequently the restricted map $P_k\alpha_{Q,M}$, after $P_kL_k\cong1$, is exactly
$$P_kP_pL_iM\cong P_rP_iL_iM\xrightarrow{P_r(u_{i,M}^{-1})}P_rM.\tag{N}$$
The first arrow is the canonical square identification for $pk=ir$. This proves (N) for the intrinsic construction, rather than choosing a new alpha by a normalization condition. Both vertical maps are proper as required by the projector lemma.

proof.text: For the base-change cube evaluate both asserted maps at $M$ on $S$ and restrict them along $k_1$. Both maps have target $L_{k_1}P_{r_1}P_cM$. For the left-hand path, $ak_1=kd$ identifies $P_{k_1}P_a\alpha_Q$ with $P_dP_k\alpha_Q$; step 3 makes it the canonical reduction to $P_dP_rM$. Step 2 applied to $\beta_k$ identifies the final restricted beta with the open-unit identification, so this path ends at $P_{r_1}P_cM$ using $rd=cr_1$. For the right-hand path use $p_1k_1=i_1r_1$: step 2 applied to $\beta_i$ identifies its restricted first factor $P_{k_1}P_{p_1}\beta_i$ with $P_{r_1}$ of that open-unit identification, and (N) for $Q_1$ identifies the last factor with the reduction to $P_{r_1}P_cM$. The initial $\theta$ on the left is the canonical identification for $bp_1=pa$, so the two starting identifications coincide: their composites express $b i_1r_1=i c r_1=i r d=p k d=p a k_1$. Both reduced maps are therefore the same unit-normalized inverse-image identification. Step 1 gives the cube equation before derivation. No base-change theorem for proper direct image is used here.

theorem singleAlpha_baseChange {V W S T V₁ W₁ S₁ T₁ : Scheme.{u}}
    (k : V ⟶ W) (i : S ⟶ T) (r : V ⟶ S) (p : W ⟶ T)
    (k₁ : V₁ ⟶ W₁) (i₁ : S₁ ⟶ T₁) (r₁ : V₁ ⟶ S₁) (p₁ : W₁ ⟶ T₁)
    (a : W₁ ⟶ W) (b : T₁ ⟶ T) (c : S₁ ⟶ S) (d : V₁ ⟶ V)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i]
    [IsOpenImmersion k₁] [IsOpenImmersion i₁]
    [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i] [QuasiCompact k₁] [QuasiCompact i₁]
    [IsProper r] [IsProper p] [IsProper r₁] [IsProper p₁]
    (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) (h₁ : k₁ ≫ p₁ = r₁ ≫ i₁)
    (wk : d ≫ k = k₁ ≫ a) (wi : c ≫ i = i₁ ≫ b)
    (wp : a ≫ p = p₁ ≫ b) (wr : d ≫ r = r₁ ≫ c)
    (sk : IsPullback d k₁ k a) (si : IsPullback c i₁ i b)
    (sp : IsPullback a p₁ p b) (sr : IsPullback d r₁ r c) :
    ∀ M : Modules B S,
      (moduleSquareG B a p₁ p b wp).hom.app ((moduleJ B i).obj M) ≫
          (modulePullback B a).map ((singleAlpha B k r p i h).app M) ≫
          (openBetaModule B d k₁ k a wk sk).hom.app ((modulePullback B r).obj M) ≫
          (moduleJ B k₁).map ((moduleSquareG B d r₁ r c wr).inv.app M) =
        (modulePullback B p₁).map ((openBetaModule B c i₁ i b wi si).hom.app M) ≫
          (singleAlpha B k₁ r₁ p₁ i₁ h₁).app ((modulePullback B c).obj M)
